newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: CS, WINTERTHUR UNDER PRESSURE ON MERGER PLANS.
newsitem.headline: CS, WINTERTHUR UNDER PRESSURE ON MERGER PLANS.

text.p: Shares in Credit Suisse Group and Winterthur Group, which announced surprise merger plans on Monday, fell in early Swiss trading after several analysts cut recommendations and profit forecasts.
CS Group registered shares were down 4.4 percent or 9.00 Swiss francs at 196.00 francs about an hour after opening.
Winterthur registered shares lost 5.2 percent or 77 francs to 1,420.
CS Group had closed 1.6 percent lower on Monday after the merger announcement and Winterthur, which gained 1.9 percent last week on takeover speculation, ended 1.1 percent lower.
Traders said there was mixed reaction to the deal, which will see CS offer 7.3 of its shares for each one of Winterthur's.
CS must issue new capital worth a nominal 1.5 billion Swiss francs, diluting earnings per share (EPS) eight percent this year and four percent in 1998.
Among reactions, traders said some brokers and banks were cutting EPS estimates, lowering recommendations or calling the price for the deal too high, although others said it was fairly priced.
Synergy effects that the companies say will total 300-350 million Swiss francs over three years were seen by some as too low to justify the merger.
Traders said the shares were also falling because the announcement of the deal put an end to weeks of speculation that had driven both shares, especially Winterthur.
Speculative investors were now looking elsewhere, they said. -- Zurich Newsroom, +41-1-631 7340
